description: Starts a Polarion asynchronous job and returns its `jobs` resource; this response means the job was accepted, not that it finished. Poll `getJob` with the returned job ID, then use `getJobLogContent` or `getJobResultFileContent` after completion. Use `run_job_and_wait` when bounded polling and a log tail are preferred. Effect: triggers a server-side action rather than a plain resource creation — whether repeating it is safe, a no-op, or rejected depends on the specific action; treat it as not guaranteed idempotent. Tip: set `dry_run: true` first to validate the arguments and preview the exact request without sending it to Polarion. The executor returns this preview as normal text, and as structured content when the tool declares an output schema.

dry_run.description: If true, validates the request and returns the exact request that would be sent to Polarion — with the Authorization header redacted and any binary payload summarized by byte length — without actually sending it.

jobId.description: Id of job factory, e.g. jobs.cleanup

params.description: Parameters of Job to be executed.

scope.description: Scope of the job. Accepted formats: 'system', 'project:{projectId}', or 'path:/{path}'.

name: executeJob
